metadata.evidence: CADET reads files in both [QDIMACS](http://www.qbflib.org/qdimacs.html) and [QAIGER](https://github.com/ltentrup/QAIGER) format. Files can be zipped with gzip, but must then end with the file extension gz or gzip.
metadata.reason: Specifies accepted input formats and compression support, needed to use the solver.

metadata.evidence:
To compile the solver type:

```bash
$ ./configure && make
```
metadata.reason: Defines the compilation step required to build the solver from source.

metadata.evidence:
To make sure the solver works correctly execute the test suite:

```bash
$ make test
```
metadata.reason: Defines how to run the test suite to verify the build.

metadata.evidence:
```bash
$ ./cadet file.qdimacs
```
metadata.reason: Primary command for running the solver on a QDIMACS file.

metadata.evidence:
You can also pipe QDIMACS into the solver:

```bash
$ cat file.qdimacs | ./cadet
```
metadata.reason: Documents an alternative invocation piping input via stdin.

metadata.evidence: With the command line option `-c [file]` CADET writes the SAT certificate for true 2QBF. You can either specify a file name to which the certificate should be written (ending in `.aag` or `.aig`) or you can specify `sdtout` to let CADET print the certificate on the terminal.
metadata.reason: Documents the command-line option for writing SAT certificates as AIGER circuits, key for result certification workflows.

metadata.evidence: To print output according to the QDIMACS standard, use the `--qdimacs_out` flag.
metadata.reason: Documents a flag controlling output format for UNSAT certificates.

metadata.evidence: To produce certificates that are compatible with [QBFcert](http://fmv.jku.at/qbfcert/) add `--qbfcert` option to the command line.
metadata.reason: Documents the option for generating QBFcert-compatible certificates.

metadata.evidence: By default CADET produces certificates that can be checked by Certcheck, which was written by [Leander Tentrup](https://www.react.uni-saarland.de/people/tentrup.html). Certcheck comes with the distribution of [CAQE](https://www.react.uni-saarland.de/tools/caqe/). To produce certificates that are compatible with [QBFcert](http://fmv.jku.at/qbfcert/) add `--qbfcert` option to the command line.
metadata.reason: Names external tools used to verify certificates, relevant for reproduction and validation.

metadata.evidence: As soon as you work with certificates you may want to install the [AIGER tool set](http://fmv.jku.at/aiger/aiger-1.9.4.tar.gz) and the [ABC](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~alanmi/abc/).
metadata.reason: External tools recommended for generating, simplifying, and checking certificates.

metadata.evidence:
```bash
$ abc -c "read result.aig; dc2; write result.aig"
```
